newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Dollar drop boosts regionals.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Dollar drop boosts regionals.

text.p: The dollar's steep drop to a near four-month low of 117.50 yen in early Monday trade boosted regional currencies, with the Singapore dollar seen gaining the most.
Dealers said dollar/Sing fell to a low of 1.4300/05, an area not seen in almost two months, from its opening 1.4380/85 before recovering to around 1.4336/46 at 0430 GMT.
Active buying of the U.S. unit by local banks near its morning low spurred speculation of intervention by the de facto central bank, pushing the U.S. dollar back above the 1.4300 area, they said.
"The local banks were buying dollars around the 1.4300/05. That's why it bounced up so fast to 1.4330/35," a European bank dealer said.
She said the U.S. unit should be supported around 1.4300 for the time being and players were likely to sell into any rallies towards the 1.4350 level.
"The market's still very long the dollar/Sing and ringgit/Sing cross so a lot of stop-losses were triggered," a U.S. bank dealer said.
The Malaysian ringgit made some headway on the dollar's weakness but its gains were restricted by dollar bids around the 2.5010/20 region, dealers said.
"I would look to buy dollar/ringgit around 2.5010/20 and sell dollar/Sing as a hedge in case the big dollar comes off more," the European bank dealer in Singapore said.
"I don't know where the big dollar is heading, whether this move has been overdone. So the ringgit/Sing cross is the most safe," she said.
But a Malaysian bank dealer said the ringgit showed scope for more gains as it had not risen in line with the dollar's slide against the yen.
In Indonesia, the rupiah gave up its early dollar-driven strength and weakened as players focused on the increasingly heated campaign for the May 29 general election, dealers said.

On Sunday, tens of thousands of supporters from the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) and loyalists of the ousted chief of the rival Indonesian Democratic Party campaigned jointly and brought Jakarta to a virtual standstill.
There were also reports of sporadic clashes from central Java, where the PPP was campaigning.

A U.S. bank dealer in Jakarta said liquidity worries had prevented players from making heavy dollar purchases despite attempts to factor in the political uncertainty hanging over the election campaign, which ends on May 23.
Spot rupiah was at 2,427.80/28.30 at 0430 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,426.5/27.5.
"The tone is a bit biddish on the dollar. But people are still worried about possible tightening on Tuesday due to weekly tax payments," the U.S. bank dealer said.
In Thailand, the baht rose in line with the weakened dollar/majors as the central bank set the mid-rate at 25.85 per dollar against 26.05 on Friday.
The baht was quoted at 25.880/25.885 to the dollar at 0430 GMT compared with 25.995/26.005 late on Friday.

"The dollar was very weak abroad. But demand for the dollar was felt this morning as some players took the opportunity (of the dollar's recent drop) to cover their short positions," a foreign bank dealer in Bangkok said.
Dealers said continued bearish sentiment for the baht after last week's sell-off on rumours of a band widening also spurred some demand for the dollar.
The central bank denied the rumours and intervened in spot and swap markets in Singapore to support the baht on Friday.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Sonali Desai in Singapore
